# CGNS C API Reference: Reading 2D Unstructured Meshes

## 0. Environment essentials

```c
#include "cgnslib.h"          /* link: -lcgns */
```
- **`cgsize_t`** — the CGNS index type (64-bit `long long` in modern builds; was `int` pre-3.1). Use it for ALL vertex/element indices.
- **1-based indexing** everywhere: zones, sections, BCs, and connectivity node references are all 1-based.
- **Return convention**: every `cg_*` function returns `int` — `0` on success (`CG_OK`), nonzero (`CG_ERROR` etc.) on failure. Always check.
- **`CGNS_ENUMT(X)`** = enum type, **`CGNS_ENUMV(X)`** = enum value (required in C++, used universally in C too, e.g. `CGNS_ENUMV(TRI_3)`).
- Coordinates and connectivity in the repo's meshes are stored **`R8`/`I8`** (double/64-bit int) — see §7.

## 1. Open file, iterate bases and zones

```c
int cg_open(const char *filename, int mode, int *fn);      /* mode: CG_MODE_READ */
int cg_close(int fn);
int cg_nbases(int fn, int *nbases);
int cg_base_read(int fn, int B, char *basename, int *cell_dim, int *phys_dim);
int cg_nzones(int fn, int B, int *nzones);
int cg_zone_type(int fn, int B, int Z, CGNS_ENUMT(ZoneType_t) *type);  /* Unstructured / Structured */
int cg_zone_read(int fn, int B, int Z, char *zonename, cgsize_t *size); /* size[3] */
int cg_nfamilies(int fn, int B, int *nfamilies);
```
- `cg_zone_read` fills `size` with `[nVertices, nCells, 0]` for an unstructured zone (2D: `size[1]` = cell count). For 2D meshes `cell_dim == 2`; `phys_dim` is 2 (planar) or 3 (surface mesh in 3D).

`cgns_reader.cpp:603-616` (internal faces) and `:637-649` (zone-interface faces) set only `face.normal.area` — never `nx`/`ny`. `Mesh::finalize()` (`cgns_reader.cpp:771-783`) only *flips* existing normals; it never computes them, and the flip test `dir.dot({nx,ny}) < 0` is `0 < 0` = false for a zero normal, so nothing happens. <task id="ses_03597be43ffeJZB925ZKmPvKtl" state="completed">
<summary>Background task completed: Oracle review of Phase 2: Partitioning & MPI</summary>
<task_result>
I've read all Phase 2 files, checked the mesh/type dependencies, and reproduced the runs (np=1 and np=4; numbers match the report: 5156/5274/5192/5194 cells, edge cut 237, symmetric send/recv counts in the CSV). Here is the review.

## Verdict

Phase 2 is **functionally correct** — the communication pattern is deadlock-free, the partition construction handles all three face types, and the index conventions are consistent. I found no outright bugs. The findings below are about **fragile contracts, test weakness, and cleanup**, ranked by importance.

---

## 1. MPI communication pattern — correct, with one fragile contract

**Deadlock-free: confirmed.** All `MPI_Irecv`s are posted before any `MPI_Isend`, then `MPI_Waitall` (halo_exchange.cpp:31-64). Fixed tag + explicit source rank is the right fix — `(source, tag)` pairs are unique. I verified the graph is guaranteed symmetric by construction: A lists B iff A has a ghost owned by B iff some A-owned cell is adjacent to a B-owned cell iff B has a ghost owned by A (partition_impl.cpp:117-125 vs 188-197), so no rank can wait on a message that will never arrive.

**Finding 1 (HIGH — silent corruption risk, correct today): the send/recv pairing has an undocumented ordering contract.** There is no pairing metadata in the exchange; `recv_cells[ni][i]` is implicitly the *i-th* element of the peer's `send_cells[ni]`. This works only because both sides happen to produce the same order:
- recv list: `ghost_set` is `std::set<Int>` → ghosts sorted ascending by global id (partition_impl.cpp:114-128, 175-178)
- send list: `send_cells_set` is `std::set<Int>` of *local* ids, and local ids are assigned in ascending global order → also ascending global id (partition_impl.cpp:188-197)

The two sets are equal by construction, so pairing is correct *today*. But nothing in halo

# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- There is NO subagent model policy on this branch: subagents may use any
  available model. No model is required, restricted, or pinned.
- Visual handoff (important): the orchestrator and other subagents are NOT
  visual-enabled. Whenever a subagent produces something visual — figures,
  plots, reports, or rendered output — hand it off to a `designer` subagent
  to check and fix visual problems before the task is considered done.

## 3. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
